page: Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the network-optimized Env6 series. It operates on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8573C processor rated up to 4.2 GHz. The instance supplies 32 virtual CPUs distributed across 16 physical cores via symmetric multithreading, alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced execution instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is fixed at 256.0 GB RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Hardware architecture does not include dedicated graphics processors or bundled local disk storage, necessitating remote network-attached disks via Azure Premium Storage for persistent data. In empirical testing, the server demonstrates strong uncached large-block read memory bandwidth at 192.86 GB/sec and strong multi-threaded decompression throughput reaching 205.46 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput also ranks within the upper 25th percentile at 56.03 GB/sec. Compute-bound tasks, such as stress-ng execution, general PassMark CPU metrics, and Redis SET operations, remain within median industry benchmarks.

The CPU-level AMX implementation provides significant acceleration for lightweight matrix workloads, achieving top-tier text generation speeds on smaller 135M language models. However, lack of discrete accelerators restricts large parameter models, where large 70B text generation yields low throughput in the bottom tier. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high RAM density per compute unit and strong network capabilities, minimizing overhead for data-heavy tiers that do not require local NVMe drives.
Workload allocation aligns with enterprise in-memory caching tiers, medium-to-large relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and memory-bound analytics engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual instance tailored for network and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz with 260 MB of L3 cache, it supplies 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 256.0 GB of system memory. The instance features hardware acceleration flags including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, but excludes local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong memory read bandwidth at 192.86 GB/sec, rapid multi-threaded decompression, and high static web serving capability, though raw multithread compute benchmarks sit near median levels. Given its high RAM-to-vCPU allocation, this VM offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-centric footprints, particularly large relational databases, in-memory caches, and enterprise data analytics requiring Premium Storage connections.
